text:
elaine: proposing a per-org rate policy sketch to handle bursts and steady usage. want feedback on RPM/TPM + concurrency + short burst windows. thinking we need enforcement at the edge + telemetry emitted for every throttle so console can show who hit limits.

chris: +1 on emitting telemetry. can we make burst windows configurable per org? some customers have bursty workloads (webhooks, batch imports)

elaine: yes. my rough policy model: RPM (requests/min), TPM (tokens/min), concurrency cap, and a burst token bucket with short refill window. example config: 
```json
{"org_id":"ORG_abc","rpm":1200,"tpm":30000,"concurrency":50,"burst":{"tokens":200,"window_seconds":60}}
```
This lets us allow short spikes while bounding steady-state throughput.

devin: question: how do we count tokens for embeddings vs text-generation? embeddings are heavy but single request. do we count by tokens in payload or a per-request weight?

elaine: proposal: two-tier accounting. primary enforcement keys off "requests" (RPM) and concurrency. token accounting (TPM) is a secondary soft throttle used for cost-aware decisions and alerts. but if TPM exceeded we also hard-throttle for safety. We need separate multipliers per endpoint: embeddings weight=3, text-gen weight=1 per 1k tokens, rerank weight=2.

aj: where does enforcement live? gateway (fast path) or a central rate-limiter service (consistent state)?

devin: central service gives consistency (per-org global view) but adds extra hop and state. gateway with local token buckets is faster but has sync issues with distributed bursts. maybe hybrid: gateway does fast local check for immediate throttling, central service does reconciliations and long-window quotas.

elaine: agreed hybrid looks best. implementation plan:
- gateway enforces RPM and concurrency with per-worker token buckets and small lease tokens for bursts.
- central quota service maintains TPM and monthly commit counters + authoritative view.
- gateway consults central for long-running overrides and can fetch per-org burst settings.

ux-sam: for console UX we should surface: current RPM/TMP usage, last throttle event (timestamp + reason), burst tokens left, and a suggested config button ("suggested burst profile"). also show per-route breakdown (embeddings vs chat).

chris: rollout plan: start with conservative defaults and opt-in per-org via console flag. monitor throttle telemetry and create regression alerts. canary on 5 orgs for two weeks.

quota-bot: deploy note: new endpoints added: POST /quota/policy (admin), GET /quota/status?org=ORG_abc (public for console). events: quota.throttle, quota.burst_refill, quota.override_applied.

aj: one more: operator controls for temporary increases (support UI) and audit log entries required. also add a config to treat internal service keys as exempt or on a separate higher quota.

elaine: action items:
- devin: prototype gateway token bucket + short lease protocol (ETA 2 weeks)
- chris: instrumentation spec for throttle events and console wireframes (ETA 1 week)
- aj: design central quota schema + admin endpoints (ETA 2 weeks)
- ux-sam: console mockups for per-org quota panel (ETA 1 week)

devin: noted. will start with a PoC that simulates burst windows under load.

elaine: thanks everyone. Ill create a doc with the config schema and link back here. if no objections by EOD well spin up the canary plan. :thumbsup:
